neighbours.label: A kin noun that follows a relative's possessive: the second link in a kinship chain ('my father's mother', 'her husband's brother'); the same possessive with a thing stays quiet
fire: We stayed with my mother's sister during the long school holidays.
He inherited the farm from his wife's father after the war.
The letter was written by her uncle's son in Canada.
My grandfather's brother emigrated to Australia in 1920.
She danced at the wedding with her sister's husband.
On Sunday we visited his father's cousin near the lake.
Their aunt's daughter moved in with the family last spring.
I keep a photo of my husband's mother on the shelf.
quiet: We stayed at my mother's cottage during the long school holidays.
He inherited the farm from his wife's employer after the war.
The letter was written on her uncle's typewriter in Canada.
My grandfather's ship sailed to Australia in 1920.
She danced at the wedding in her sister's shoes.
On Sunday we visited his father's shop near the lake.
Their aunt's dog moved in with the family last spring.
I keep a photo of my husband's boat on the shelf.

short: second kin noun in a kinship chain
notes: Card: ' mother' x3, ' father' x2, ' child' x2, also ' cell', ' morning', ' defendant', ' artwork', which this does not explain, so likely partial. Probe: father's mother 0.71, husband's brother 0.54, bride's father 0.37, king's sister 0.22; but neighbour's daughter 0.11 and boy's mother 0.06, so the possessor being a relative seems to matter, and I am not sure of it. Things after the possessive 0.03-0.09.
